exposure: operative vaginal births assisted by manual rotation
outcome: admission to the special care baby unit
cohort: 2,426 women with operative births complicated with malposition of the fetal head in the second stage of labour
finding: Adverse neonatal and maternal outcomes associated with successful manual rotations followed by direct traction instruments were comparable to traditional methods of operative births.
mod_finding: Operative vaginal births assisted by manual rotation followed by direct traction instruments resulted in similar rates of adverse neonatal and maternal outcomes compared to other methods of rotational births, including cesarean section.
